offer_letter.markdown:
# Offer of employment — Senior Legal Counsel: Regulatory and Privacy

## 1. Job Offer: Senior Legal Counsel: Regulatory and Privacy

Dear {{employee.full_name}},

We are pleased to offer you the position of Senior Legal Counsel: Regulatory and Privacy at Absa Group. This is a permanent role. Your employment will start on 1 December 2026.

## 2. Your Role

You will give specialist legal advice on data privacy, data protection, regulatory and financial crime matters. You will review privacy impact assessments, new products and projects, and draft and negotiate data protection and privacy agreements. You will also work with stakeholders across the business, manage external counsel, and help manage legal risk across the business.

## 3. Where and When You Will Work

Your place of work will be Johannesburg, head office. Your ordinary hours of work are 40 hours per week, 8 hours per day over 5 days a week, Monday to Friday from 08:00 to 17:00. You will take a 60 minute meal break after no more than five hours of continuous work. Your first 3 months of employment will be a probationary period.

## 4. Your Pay

You will be paid R18,000.00 per month as your basic salary. This is paid monthly on the 25th by EFT. PAYE and UIF of 1% will be deducted from your pay.

## 5. Next Steps

Please bring your ID and qualifications when you confirm this offer. This offer expires on 2026-11-30. If you have questions, contact us at hr@example.co.za.

To accept this offer, please sign and date it below by {{date_signed}}.

Review and legally assess Privacy Impact Assessments, compliance assessments, new products, projects, technologies, processes and proposed data-use arrangements.; Provide independent legal advice on novel and complex data use, data sharing, disclosure, retention, cross-border transfer and related privacy matters across the Bank, the Group and ARO.; Draft, review and negotiate data protection provisions, data processing and data sharing agreements, consent wording, privacy notices, forms, customer communications and other privacy-related documentation.; Build strong client relationships and engage confidently with stakeholders at different levels of seniority, managing complex or conflicting expectations professionally and effectively.; Independently plan, prioritise and manage a broad portfolio of matters from instruction through to completion, taking ownership and providing clear legal advice, direction and follow-up.; Contribute to the development and achievement of team objectives and strategy, while providing high-quality support to business and Legal stakeholders.; Represent the Bank independently as a subject-matter expert at internal committees, governance forums, industry engagements and professional bodies, and supervise others where appropriate.; Demonstrate strong analytical skills and solve complex problems creatively and effectively; Drive good cost-control behaviour, particularly in relation to external legal spend, and consistently deliver against a broad range of competing priorities and deadlines.; Manage external counsel; Add value in commercial and technical discussions, translate complex privacy requirements into practical business advice, and provide relevant legal training to internal clients.; Strengthen Legal’s contribution to the effective identification, management and mitigation of legal risk across the business.; Promote awareness of, and support adherence to, applicable legal policies and control requirements.; Build effective partnerships with Risk, Compliance and other key control functions to support coordinated and effective risk management.; Collaborate proactively across teams and geographies within Legal, contributing to the development and achievement of team objectives and helping to break down silos.; Share knowledge and expertise openly, provide objective and constructive feedback, and contribute to the planning and delivery of Legal Function knowledge sessions.; Act as a trusted legal advisor to business and infrastructure functions, providing clear, practical advice on relevant legal and market developments and their business impact.; Proactively monitor domestic and international privacy and regulatory developments, assess their legal and practical impact on the Bank, the Group and ARO, and communicate implications and recommended actions clearly and timeously.; Represent the Bank as a subject-matter expert at internal committees and industry forums, contributing to industry initiatives and maintaining a strong external professional network.. # Contract of employment — Senior Legal Counsel: Regulatory and Privacy

## 1. Parties

This contract of employment is entered into between Absa Group, of 1 Main Road, Johannesburg (the Employer), and {{employee.full_name}}, identity number {{employee.id_number}}, of {{employee.address}} (the Employee).

## 2. Position and duties

The Employer appoints the Employee as Senior Legal Counsel: Regulatory and Privacy. The Employee's duties include: To provide highly specialised legal advice and support to the dedicated area of support.; Act as a senior legal subject-matter expert on data privacy and data protection law, regulatory and financial crime.; Review and legally assess Privacy Impact Assessments, compliance assessments, new products, projects, technologies, processes and proposed data-use arrangements.; Provide independent legal advice on novel and complex data use, data sharing, disclosure, retention, cross-border transfer and related privacy matters across the Bank, the Group and ARO.; Draft, review and negotiate data protection provisions, data processing and data sharing agreements, consent wording, privacy notices, forms, customer communications and other privacy-related documentation.; Build strong client relationships and engage confidently with stakeholders at different levels of seniority, managing complex or conflicting expectations professionally and effectively.; Independently plan, prioritise and manage a broad portfolio of matters from instruction through to completion, taking ownership and providing clear legal advice, direction and follow-up.; Contribute to the development and achievement of team objectives and strategy, while providing high-quality support to business and Legal stakeholders.; Represent the Bank independently as a subject-matter expert at internal committees, governance forums, industry engagements and professional bodies, and supervise others where appropriate.; Demonstrate strong analytical skills and solve complex problems creatively and effectively; Drive good cost-control behaviour, particularly in relation to external legal spend, and consistently deliver against a broad range of competing priorities and deadlines.; Manage external counsel; Add value in commercial and technical discussions, translate complex privacy requirements into practical business advice, and provide relevant legal training to internal clients.; Strengthen Legal’s contribution to the effective identification, management and mitigation of legal risk across the business.; Promote awareness of, and support adherence to, applicable legal policies and control requirements.; Build effective partnerships with Risk, Compliance and other key control functions to support coordinated and effective risk management.; Collaborate proactively across teams and geographies within Legal, contributing to the development and achievement of team objectives and helping to break down silos.; Share knowledge and expertise openly, provide objective and constructive feedback, and contribute to the planning and delivery of Legal Function knowledge sessions.; Act as a trusted legal advisor to business and infrastructure functions, providing clear, practical advice on relevant legal and market developments and their business impact.; Proactively monitor domestic and international privacy and regulatory developments, assess their legal and practical impact on the Bank, the Group and ARO, and communicate implications and recommended actions clearly and timeously.; Represent the Bank as a subject-matter expert at internal committees and industry forums, contributing to industry initiatives and maintaining a strong external professional network.. The Employer may reasonably require the Employee to perform other duties consistent with the position.

## 3. Commencement

Employment commences on 1 December 2026 on a permanent basis.

## 4. Probation

The first 3 month(s) of employment are a probationary period during which the Employer will assess the Employee's performance against the requirements of the position and give reasonable evaluation, instruction, training, guidance or counselling where needed. Confirmation, extension or termination at the end of probation will follow a fair procedure.

## 5. Place of work

The Employee's place of work is Johannesburg, head office.

## 6. Hours of work

The Employee's ordinary hours of work are 40 hours per week, 8 hours per day over 5 days per week (Mon–Fri 08:00–17:00). A meal interval of 60 minutes is taken after no more than five hours of continuous work. The Employee is entitled to a daily rest period of at least 12 consecutive hours and a weekly rest period of at least 36 consecutive hours.

## 7. Remuneration

The Employee will be paid R18,000.00 per month (basic salary), equivalent to R103.85 per ordinary hour, payable monthly on the 25th by EFT. No other cash payments are payable. No payments in kind are made.

## 8. Overtime

Overtime is worked only by agreement and may not exceed ten hours in any week. Overtime is paid at 1.5 times the Employee's ordinary hourly wage, or, by agreement, compensated with paid time off. Work on a Sunday is paid at double the ordinary wage (or one and a half times if the Employee ordinarily works on Sundays), and work on a public holiday at double the ordinary wage.

## 9. Deductions

The following deductions will be made from the Employee's remuneration: PAYE; UIF 1%. No other deduction will be made without the Employee's written agreement in respect of a specific debt, or as required by law, a court order or an arbitration award.

## 10. Leave

The Employee is entitled to 15 working days of paid annual leave per annual leave cycle of 12 months, to be taken at a time agreed with the Employer and not later than six months after the end of the cycle. Sick leave: 30 days' paid sick leave in every 36-month cycle (during the first six months, one day for every 26 days worked); a medical certificate may be required for absences of more than two consecutive days or on more than two occasions in eight weeks. Maternity leave: at least 4 consecutive months. Parental leave: 10 consecutive days. Adoption and commissioning parental leave as provided in the Act. Family responsibility leave: 3 days' paid leave per year once employed for longer than four months and for at least four days a week.

## 11. Termination and notice

Either party may terminate this contract on written notice of one week if the employee has been employed for six months or less; two weeks if employed for more than six months but not more than one year; four weeks if employed for more than one year. Notice may not be given during any period of leave. Nothing in this clause prevents the Employer from terminating employment summarily for a fair reason following a fair procedure, or the parties from agreeing to waive notice.

## 12. Bargaining council or sectoral determination

No bargaining council agreement or sectoral determination applies to the Employer's business.

## 13. Confidentiality

The Employee will not, during or after employment, disclose or use any confidential information of the Employer, its clients or suppliers, except as required to perform the Employee's duties or by law.

## 14. Other documents

No other documents form part of this contract.

## 15. General

This contract records the whole agreement between the parties on its subject; any amendment must be in writing and signed by both parties. Where any term is less favourable to the Employee than the Basic Conditions of Employment Act or an applicable sectoral determination or collective agreement, the more favourable provision applies. The Employer will keep these particulars for three years after termination and will explain them to the Employee on request.

plain_language.explanation: This clause names the two people entering the contract: Absa Group, based at 1 Main Road, Johannesburg, and you, the Employee. It records your identity number and address as part of the agreement.

You are appointed as Senior Legal Counsel: Regulatory and Privacy, and your job covers the listed duties, which focus on data privacy, data protection and regulatory legal advice, drafting agreements, managing external counsel and supporting the business on legal risk. The Employer can also ask you to do other reasonable tasks that fit with this role.
Your employment starts on 1 December 2026. It is a permanent job, meaning it does not have a fixed end date.

Your first 3 months are a probation period, during which the Employer will check how well you are doing the job. The Employer must give you fair guidance and support during this time, and any decision to confirm, extend or end your employment after probation must follow a fair process.
You will work at the Johannesburg head office.

You will work 40 hours a week, 8 hours a day, 5 days a week, from Monday to Friday, 08:00 to 17:00. You get a 60-minute meal break after working no more than five hours in a row. You are also entitled to at least 12 hours of rest between workdays and at least 36 hours of rest each week.

You will earn R18,000.00 a month as your basic salary, which works out to R103.85 per hour. You are paid once a month, on the 25th, by electronic transfer into your bank account. You will not receive any other cash payments or payments in goods or services.

You only work overtime if you agree to it, and it cannot be more than 10 hours in a week. Overtime pay is 1.5 times your normal hourly rate, or you and the Employer can agree to paid time off instead. Working on a Sunday is paid double your normal wage, unless you normally work Sundays, in which case it is 1.5 times your wage; working on a public holiday is always paid double.

Your employer will deduct PAYE (income tax) and 1% for UIF from your salary. No other money can be taken from your pay unless you agree to it in writing for a specific debt, or the law, a court, or an arbitrator requires it.

You get 15 working days of paid annual leave each year, which you take at a time agreed with your employer, and must use within six months after the leave year ends. You get 30 days of paid sick leave every 36 months, though in your first six months you earn one sick day for every 26 days worked; your employer can ask for a doctor's note if you are off for more than two days in a row or more than twice in eight weeks. You can take at least 4 months of maternity leave and 10 days of parental leave, plus adoption or commissioning parental leave as the law allows. After four months of employment, working at least four days a week, you also get 3 days of paid family responsibility leave each year.

Either you or your employer can end the contract with written notice: one week's notice if you have worked six months or less, two weeks if you have worked between six months and a year, and four weeks if you have worked more than a year. Notice cannot be given while you are on leave. Your employer can still dismiss you immediately for a serious reason, but only after following a fair process, and both sides can agree to skip the notice period.
No bargaining council agreement or sectoral determination applies to this employer's business, so none of those extra rules apply to your job.

You must not share or use confidential information belonging to the Employer, its clients or suppliers, either while working there or after you leave. The only exceptions are when you need the information to do your job or when the law requires you to disclose it.
No other documents are part of this contract besides what is written here.

This contract is the entire agreement between you and your employer, and any changes must be written down and signed by both of you. If any part of this contract gives you less than what the Basic Conditions of Employment Act, a sectoral determination, or a collective agreement requires, the better terms will apply instead. Your employer will keep your employment records for three years after you leave, and will explain these terms to you if you ask.

This is the signature block. The Employer's representative, {{employer.signatory}}, signs on behalf of Absa Group, and you, {{employee.full_name}}, sign as the Employee, both at the place and on the date shown.
